independence_declaration.statement: domain-reviewer authored no DG3 implementation, test, register row or ADR in the reviewed candidate, including the round-5 repair T-DG3-KBE-G (commit 10472b4). I formed this verdict from my own runs in a complete (non-shallow) disposable clone of source commit 21e2742. I used my own probes from rounds 3-4 (dg3-api, dg3-api-extra, dg3-ui-world, dg3-ui, dg3-ui-inherited, dg3-ui-overflow, dg3-ui-overflow-r3), with only the round label and evidence path changed. I read the repair diff only to understand the change. I did not open any other reviewer's round-5 record or evidence.

checks_run.environment: Repository /home/user/My-owns at HEAD 40c84e8; git clone into $TMPDIR/review-dom checked out at 21e2742e4b0f6800e379a4d935d5592a873b1c59; Node 24.21.0.
checks_run.expected: candidate_id sha256:dfedd62f…689ed3 over 757 files in both trees. The freeze HEAD differs from source only by delivery records.
checks_run.actual: The assignment hash matches (20cd1684…2599). HEAD is 40c84e8, the round-5 freeze commit. source_commit 21e2742 is its parent, and that commit changes only the three round-5 assignments, the candidate manifest, progress.md and stages.json, none of them in the manifest. The candidate ID is sha256:dfedd62f05412fd7888b7d13d2391c6ab5df7d56563ab946502e53c558689ed3 with 757 files in the repository and in the clone before the runs. The clone is not shallow, and the installed lockfile is byte-identical to pnpm-lock.yaml. Disclosure: one post-run recompute in the clone gave sha256:68d0332c… over 764 files. The cause was my own untracked rv/ directory, the 7 probe .mjs copies that run-all.sh puts in the clone so @playwright/test resolves (git status: '?? rv/'). After I moved rv/ out, git status was clean and the recompute gave dfedd62f… with 757 files again. The repository's recompute after the runs is also dfedd62f… with 757 files.

checks_run.actual: 'PASS register rules at DG3', 'PASS gate DG2 (historical)' and 'PASS gate DG1 (historical)', each with exit 0.

checks_run.procedure: In the clone, run typecheck, build, lint, the unit tests (pnpm test: unit-node + unit-web, then unit-formula-nocodegen) and the contrast check, on Node 22 and on Node 24.
checks_run.command: bash docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG3/domain/round-5/checks.sh (pnpm -r typecheck; pnpm -r build; pnpm lint; pnpm test; pnpm --filter @mth/design-tokens run check:contrast)
checks_run.environment: Disposable clone at 21e2742; node_modules copied with cp -a from the working tree (lockfile identical); Node 22.22.2 and 24.21.0; offline sandbox.
checks_run.expected: All exit 0 on both versions. Every skip or warning is explained.
checks_run.actual: Every step exits 0 on both versions (checks-run.out: ALLDONE). pnpm test: 81 files, 1614/1614 passed (unit-node + unit-web), then 3 files, 220 passed and 1 skipped of 221 (unit-formula-nocodegen). Round 4 had 1593 and 199+1. The growth is exactly the repair's fuzz.test.ts, which grew from 50 to 71 tests (the W1/W2/W4/W5, catch, finally, async and X1 probe rows), and that file is counted in both projects. Lint runs with --max-warnings=0 and exits 0, so the new catch-shape, EvalError, synchronous-engine and no-unsafe-finally rules accept the five engine catches. Disclosures: (1) The ONE skipped test is fuzz.test.ts 'every file of the engine's import closure gets the engine-source lint rules', declared it.skipIf(NOCODEGEN). ESLint compiles its rule schemas with ajv (new Function), so it cannot run under --disallow-code-generation-from-strings. It RAN and passed in unit-node (71/71 on both versions). This is the documented exception in ADR-0024 §6. (2) The build logs carry Vite's 'Some chunks are larger than 500 kB … chunkSizeWarningLimit' advisory for apps/web, the same as rounds 1-4. It is a size notice, not an error. (3) The contrast logs' 'error' matches are token names (feedback.error.*) on PASS lines. (4) The 'warn' grep hit in the lint logs is the command line '--max-warnings=0'. No failed, flaky or timed-out test.

checks_run.procedure: Inspect git diff 171a0b57..21e2742 outside docs/delivery. Classify every changed line of the engine's non-test sources. Confirm that no API, web, DB, shared-schema or i18n file changed. Check whether EvalFailure/ParseFailure could be EvalError subclasses, because evaluate.ts reorders two checks.
checks_run.command: bash docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG3/domain/round-5/hygiene.sh; git diff 171a0b57..21e2742 -- packages/shared/src eslint.config.js docs/architecture; grep -n 'class EvalFailure|class ParseFailure' packages/shared/src/formula
checks_run.environment: Repository at HEAD 40c84e8 (the source tree is identical to 21e2742).
checks_run.expected: T-DG3-KBE-G only: the EvalError-rethrow rule enforced in lint and the scan, parse.ts given the same catch guard, and ADR-0024 §6 corrected. No change to formula semantics.
checks_run.actual: 7 files: ADR-0024, p3-work-split.md (amendment 27), eslint.config.js (the catch-shape, EvalError-only-after-instanceof and synchronous-engine selectors, plus no-unsafe-finally), and packages/shared/src/formula/{evaluate.ts, index.ts (comment only), parse.ts, fuzz.test.ts}. The behavioural lines in non-test sources are: (a) evaluate.ts moves 'if (e instanceof EvalError) throw e;' ahead of 'if (e instanceof EvalFailure) return fail(...)'. EvalFailure is a plain class ('class EvalFailure {', evaluate.ts:91) and not an Error or EvalError subclass, so no value can match both tests and the order changes nothing. (b) parse.ts adds 'if (e instanceof EvalError) throw e;' ahead of the ParseFailure check. Its old final 'throw e' already rethrew anything that was not a ParseFailure, and ParseFailure is a plain class (parse.ts:41), so the behaviour is identical. The repair changed no tokenizer, parser grammar, type checker, period/unit rule, rounding or decimal operation. No file under apps/, packages/db or packages/shared/src/schemas changed, and there is no i18n change. The commit log 171a0b57..21e2742 contains only T-DG3-KBE-G (10472b4, merged in af27b01) plus delivery-record and review-evidence commits. Seeded results unchanged on the live stack (DOM-R5-07): attach rate 0.10->0.12 × 100000 × ARPU 50 SAR = '100000' exact (rounded false); the cost example gives 500000; monthly × annual gives 422 formula.period_mismatch.

At each state it checks the inheritedApproval annotation (status, counts), G1 in the list and the view, and the gate_submission/gate_decision row counts.

checks_run.actual: 33/33 PASS, exit 0, with the same ids as round 4. The annotation goes pending_verification/false, accepted/true, accepted/false once the evidence is unverified, accepted/true again, then revoked/false and rejected/false. In every state G1 is draft, with approvedAt null, latestSubmissionNo 0, and 0 gate_submission and 0 gate_decision rows. summary: PASS. I recomputed the candidate ID on a complete clone: dfedd62f…, 757 files. The KBE-G repair changes only lint and scan rules, tests, ADR text, one reordered rethrow in evaluate.ts and one added rethrow in parse.ts. Neither engine change alters behaviour, because EvalFailure and ParseFailure are plain classes. Formula semantics are therefore unchanged: 100000 SAR exact, the cost example gives 500000, and monthly × annual is refused. F-DG3-120 still holds (33/33 API, 94/94 UI: the annotation states and counts are correct, and G1 stays draft with no decision). F-DG3-170 still holds (12/12 and 155/155: the badge wraps inside its card and row in EN and AR). The full domain probes match round 4 exactly (API 139/139, UI 42/42, the same ids). Unit tests pass on Node 22 and 24 (1614 + 220 passed, 1 documented skip), the targeted integration suites pass (156), and all three validators pass. No new finding.
